inline_comments.comment: `MaskedMTKNPT.__init__` calls `MolecularDynamics.__init__` directly instead of `super().__init__()`, bypassing `MTKNPT.__init__` entirely. This causes roughly 30 lines of initialization code — thermostat/barostat setup, the constraints check, `_num_atoms_global`, `_temperature_K`, `_pressure_au`, `_kT`, `_q`, `_p`, `_h` — to be duplicated verbatim. Any future change to `MTKNPT.__init__` (e.g., a new validation or attribute) will silently not apply to `MaskedMTKNPT`. The fix is to set `self._mask = mask` before calling `super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)`, which works because `MTKNPT.__init__` already accesses `self.mask` via a property. Use `super().__init__()` (the project style rule) rather than naming the parent directly.

`get_conserved_energy` uses `self.atoms.get_total_energy()`. Per the project rule, conserved-quantity methods must compute `atoms.get_potential_energy(force_consistent=True)` plus kinetic energy derived from momenta, not `get_total_energy()`. `get_total_energy()` can return inconsistent values for some calculators (e.g., those that distinguish SCF and force-consistent energies), which would produce a spurious drift in the conserved quantity and make the conservation test unreliable. The sibling class `NoseHooverChainNVT.get_conserved_energy` already uses `get_potential_energy(force_consistent=True) + get_kinetic_energy()` as the correct pattern.

`self._h0_basis` is computed once from the initial cell and never updated. As the simulation runs, `_integrate_q_cell` (inherited from `MTKNPT`) modifies `self._h` at every step. Two things break as the cell drifts from its initial shape: (1) the `_p_g` property reconstructs the 3×3 tensor using stale initial unit vectors, so the eigenvector decomposition in `_integrate_q` and `_integrate_q_cell` no longer aligns with the intended mask directions; (2) the stress projection in `_integrate_p_cell` (`np.outer(self._h0_basis[c], self._h0_basis[c])`) uses initial-frame axes rather than the current cell axes, accumulating physical error for long runs. Either recompute `_h0_basis` from the current `self._h` at the start of each `_integrate_p_cell` call, or clearly document in the class docstring that the implementation assumes small cell deformations and that the masked axes are defined relative to the initial cell.

`raise AttributeError()` has no message. If this setter is ever triggered unexpectedly — for example by a future refactor that calls `self._p_g = ...` in the parent without knowing about the override, or by internal numpy operations — the traceback gives no clue about why or how to fix it. At minimum provide a descriptive message: `raise AttributeError("_p_g is read-only in MaskedMTKNPT; update _p_c directly instead.")`.

The comma separating the list argument from `axis=0` is placed on its own line (`]\n            ,`). Standard Python formatting puts the comma after `]` on the same line: `],`. This is visually confusing and will fail `ruff format`.

The `mask` parameter is inserted between `pressure_au` and `tdamp`, breaking the parameter order used by all sibling NPT classes (`IsotropicMTKNPT`, `MTKNPT`), which list all thermo/baro parameters together after the physics scalars. As a keyword-only argument (enforced naturally by the `*args, **kwargs` delegation pattern that should replace the duplicated `__init__`), `mask` can follow `pdamp` without impacting call sites, keeping the signature consistent with the parent.

The class docstring uses a plain backtick cross-reference: `` See also `NoseHooverChainNVT` ``. ASE RST conventions require the `:class:` role: `` See also :class:`NoseHooverChainNVT` ``. Without the role, Sphinx renders this as literal text rather than a hyperlink.

`test_masked_npt` has no docstring. Per the project rule, test functions that verify a physical invariant must include a docstring naming that invariant explicitly (e.g., "Verify that MaskedMTKNPT conserves the MTK extended-system energy and enforces the cell-axis mask."). The function name alone does not convey what physical property is being asserted.

The test checks that the conserved energy is preserved and that positions changed, but it never verifies that the mask actually constrains the cell. For example, for `mask=(False, False, True)` the a and b cell lengths should remain unchanged while c changes. Without an assertion like `assert np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(atoms.get_cell()[0]), initial_a_length)` for each non-masked axis, a bug that ignores the mask entirely (e.g., an off-by-one in the mask loop) would pass all three existing assertions. This is the primary behavioral guarantee of the new class and must be explicitly tested.

When `mask` is not `None` (uniaxial, biaxial, iso cases), `test_anisotropic_barostat` still passes a 3×3 symmetric `p_g` array to `MTKBarostat.integrate_nhc_baro`. However, `MaskedMTKNPT._integrate_p_cell_by_barostat` passes a 1D `_p_c` array of shape `(3,)`. While `np.sum(p_cell**2)` is shape-agnostic, the round-trip test with a 3×3 input does not cover the actual code path used in production. Add a parallel test branch that initializes `p_c` as a shape-`(3,)` array when `mask` is not `None`, matching the real usage.

RST formatting bug: the bullet reads `` `MaskedMTKNPT`` `` — one opening backtick and two closing backticks. This is malformed RST and will render incorrectly. Use the Sphinx cross-reference role instead: `:class:`MaskedMTKNPT``. Additionally, the entry is missing the required `:mr:`NNNN`` merge-request reference at the end of the bullet.

general_comments.comment: `MaskedMTKNPT` is not registered in `doc/ase/md.rst`. Per the project rule, every new MD dynamics class must have an `.. autoclass::` directive added in the appropriate ensemble section (NPT here) and a brief mention in any summary or recommendation text. Without this, the class is invisible to users consulting the documentation.

For non-orthogonal cells (e.g., the `hcp_Cu` fixture used in tests, which has a non-orthogonal c-axis relative to a/b), the masked dynamics may produce unexpected coupling between cell axes. The reconstructed `_p_g` tensor — a sum of `p_c * e_c ⊗ e_c` over masked axes — has eigenvectors that align with the masked cell axes only when those axes are mutually orthogonal. For non-orthogonal cells, `np.linalg.eigh(_p_g)` in `_integrate_q_cell` will mix directions, causing the cell to deform in directions beyond the intended mask. This physical limitation should be documented in the class docstring (e.g., "Currently most reliable for orthorhombic or nearly orthorhombic cells").

The `_integrate_p_cell_by_barostat` hook added to `MTKNPT` is a clean abstraction that enables the `MaskedMTKNPT` override. However, the analogous method `_init_cell_momenta` hook (which would initialize `_p_g` vs `_p_c`) is absent from the diff's `MaskedMTKNPT`, meaning cell-momenta initialization is inline in `__init__` rather than following the same hook pattern. If the final design uses `super().__init__()`, a `_init_cell_momenta` override (as exists in the post-review file) is the right approach and should be included here for structural consistency.
